chunks: As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Ṣabbāḥ together, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
Do not touch the muṣḥaf without taharah, nor in the state of janabah, and do not touch its script, and do not suspend it.
Indeed, Allah, Exalted is He, says: “None touch it except the purified.”
So the proper way regarding this report is that we interpret it as indicating a type of karahah rather than prohibition.

key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: dislikedness; an act considered reprehensible but not forbidden
key_terms.الْمُصْحَفُ: the written codex of the Qur'an
key_terms.جُنُبًا: being in a state of janabah requiring ghusl

ai.seo_question: Is it forbidden for a junub person to touch the muṣḥaf in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling on touching the muṣḥaf and its writing while lacking taharah or being in the state of janabah. It cites the Qur’anic phrase “لَا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ” and concludes that the report is to be understood as indicating karahah rather than strict prohibition.
